description: Standalone local-first provider and model registry with Ollama discovery, encrypted API Stuff intake, health receipts, persistence, import, export, and an optional Hearthgate adapter.

hierarchy.inheritance: Universal Horizon is the sky. Hearthfire: Arkfire and Hearthgate: Arkfire 0.002 operate beneath it and do not supersede it. This module runs on its own and may connect to either host through an optional, reversible adapter.

hostAdapters.disconnectBehaviour: The standalone module continues running and retains its own data.

consentRequirements.note: MF-001.1 does not send prompts or project content to providers.
The desktop shell reads only the selected file, encrypts recognised credentials with Electron safeStorage, and exposes only secret-free metadata to the renderer and registry.

networkRequirements.purpose: Reach configured Ollama endpoints for health and model discovery.

deviceRequirements.purpose: Native API Stuff import requires the Electron desktop shell and OS-backed safeStorage. No plaintext fallback is permitted.

lifecycle.install: Run the NSIS installer or unpack the portable ZIP.
lifecycle.launchStandalone: Launch Arkfire Model Foundry or run npm start.
lifecycle.enableInHost: Connect the optional adapter to the module base URL.
lifecycle.pause: Stop issuing probes; the service remains readable.
lifecycle.disableInHost: Disable the host adapter without stopping the module.
lifecycle.removeFromHost: Delete only the host adapter record.
lifecycle.uninstallStandalone: Use Windows Apps or remove the portable directory.
lifecycle.restore: Install or unpack again, then import a prior export bundle. Encrypted credentials remain machine/user-bound and are not exported.

importProcedure: Use Import API Stuff.txt in the desktop application for encrypted credential classification, or POST an arkfire.model-foundry-export/v1 bundle to /api/import for secret-free registry restoration.
exportProcedure: GET /api/export or use Export Registry in the standalone UI. Exports contain the complete health receipt history and no credentials.
healthChecks: registry store is readable and writable
each configured Ollama provider reports available or unavailable honestly
cloud-routed model tags are not labelled device-local
mutating HTTP routes require same-origin CSRF validation
acceptanceTests: launch with Hearthfire and Hearthgate absent
classify cloud-routed Ollama tags as external-processing-possible
report an unavailable endpoint without crashing
serialize concurrent registry mutations without lost updates
export the full registry and receipt history
merge imported receipts without erasing the local audit trail
parse API Stuff labels without placing raw secrets in registry or export structures
report duplicate API Stuff labels and use the last occurrence deterministically
build an unsigned Windows NSIS installer and portable ZIP

provenance.contribution: Existing four-port Ollama health probing inspected and preserved as source lineage.
provenance.author: Boxfire

provenance.contribution: Existing model endpoint and model-name definitions inspected; dispatch remains untouched during MF-001 extraction.
User-owned plaintext source format for provider and bridge credential labels. Raw values remain outside repository, renderer, exports, and logs.
Installer conventions reused without creating a runtime dependency on Hearthgate.

knownLimitations: MF-001.1 discovers and records models but does not invoke them.
Imported cloud provider profiles remain disabled and invocation-locked until MF-002 adds explicit route consent.
Ollama tags containing cloud are marked as potentially externally processed; the Foundry does not invoke them in this milestone.
HydraDB, Supabase, and Notion credentials are classified for a future Bridges module but are not connected by Model Foundry.
Encrypted credentials are bound to the current operating-system user and are deliberately absent from registry exports.
The Hearthgate adapter contract is present but host-side installation is not yet implemented.
Installer builds are unsigned until code signing is configured.
The module remains PARTIAL until CI and a second reviewer provide standalone and packaging receipts.
